newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen testing higher on sound GDP.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen testing higher on sound GDP.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to test higher on Monday on sound first-quarter economic and corporate performances despite a rise in the index for the last six sessions, brokers said.

Taiwan's first-quarter gross domestic product likely will rise around 6.6 percent, up from a February forecast of 6.4 percent, the cabinet's Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Monday.
On Saturday, the index ended up 7.53 points or 0.09 percent at 8,661.72. A 8,600-8,750 range was seen for Monday.

"Everybody knows that the index had risen for six straight days, but sentiment should still be bullish on a higher-than-expected first-quarter GDP growth," said Michael Hung, an independent senior analyst.
"Also, first-quarter corporate earnings, especially the electronics sector, really had shown signs of recovery," Hung said.
